Every line of Triple Red 7s Multiplier's prize table below shows today's count, not last month's.
802.headline: The prize table, line by line

803.body:
About a third of the tickets for "Triple Red 777s" are sold. The top prize count has held, with three of five still unclaimed. The number of tickets printed is fixed, so that is a plain good sign.

If "Triple Red 777s" is your usual pick, check this page often. The prize counts change even when the ticket looks the same.
803.headline: Tickets sell, top prizes remain

804.body:
"Diamond Bingo" has five of seven top prizes left and is in the middle of its run. About a quarter of the tickets are already sold. As a game goes on, the same prizes are spread across fewer tickets. Right now, tickets and top prizes are running out at about the same rate.

If "Diamond Bingo" is your usual pick, check this page often. The prize counts change even when the ticket looks the same.
804.headline: Where this game is in its run

805.body: The big board on "Multiply Your Money" just moved: five $50,000 top prizes were claimed two weeks ago, leaving four of the original seven still out there. Everything below the top tier is still in play — this page has the full count. If "Multiply Your Money" is your usual pick, make this page a habit — the board moves even when the ticket art doesn't.
805.headline: Scratch one big winner off the list

806.body:
"Win $50, $100 or $200" is near the midpoint of its run, with about half of its tickets still unsold. Late in a run, a game is worth a look when prizes outlast tickets. Early on, the prize design matters most. Here, tickets and top prizes are running out at about the same rate.

Every line of Win $50, $100 or $200's prize table below shows today's count, not last month's.
806.headline: How far along this game is

807.body:
"Ravens X2" has 293,535 prizes of $2 still unclaimed, which is its most common win. Just below the top prize is the $5,000 prize, with three left. The full count for every prize level is listed below.

The table below shows the full count for "Ravens X2", with every prize level included.
807.headline: Prize table details

808.body:
"Ravens X10" is in the middle of its run, with about two-thirds of its tickets still unsold. Late in a run, a game is worth a look when prizes outlast tickets. Early on, the prize design matters most. Here, neither the tickets nor the top prizes are running out faster than the other.

The table below shows the full count for "Ravens X10", with every prize level included.
808.headline: Where this game is in its run

809.body:
About a quarter of the tickets for "Gold Bar Bingo" are sold. The top prize count has held, with six of seven still unclaimed. The number of tickets printed is fixed, so that is a plain good sign.

The numbers for "Gold Bar Bingo" are recalculated every morning, and this page changes with them.
809.headline: No new top prize claims

810.body:
"In the Green" has gone over a month without a top prize claim, and tickets kept selling. Only a fixed number of tickets are printed. About a third of the tickets are sold, and every remaining $50,000 prize is still unclaimed. That leaves the same top prizes among fewer tickets.

The table below shows the full count for "In the Green", with every prize level included.
810.headline: Top prizes are still unclaimed

811.body:
"Extreme Green" can match another game on price and top prize and still pay out very differently. This game is a game that pays many small prizes and few large ones. Of its unclaimed prize money, about three-quarters is in wins under $5,000 and the rest is in bigger prizes. Neither kind is better, and each suits different players.

Today's free summary of "Extreme Green" ends here. Every number behind it is on this page.
811.headline: The prize mix in this game

812.body:
A $1,000 top prize on "Loose Change®" was claimed last week. The game started with 24 top prizes and has nineteen top prizes left. The prize table on this page has today's count for every prize level.

If "Loose Change®" is your usual pick, check this page often. The prize counts change even when the ticket looks the same.
812.headline: A top prize was just claimed

814.body:
A $100,000 top prize on "High Voltage" was claimed earlier this week. The game started with eight top prizes and has seven top prizes left. The prize table on this page has today's count for every prize level.

The numbers for "High Voltage" are recalculated every morning, and this page changes with them.
814.headline: Someone claimed a $100,000 prize

815.body:
About a quarter of the tickets for "$100,000 Crossword" are sold. The top prize count has held, with nine of nine still unclaimed. The number of tickets printed is fixed, so that is a plain good sign.

Every line of $100,000 Crossword's prize table below shows today's count, not last month's.
815.headline: Over a month, no top prize claimed

816.body:
"Deluxe Crossword" is new from the Maryland Lottery. It is a $5 game with eight top prizes of $50,000. Nothing big has been won yet because almost no one has played it. This page will show it when that changes.

The numbers for "Deluxe Crossword" will change a little by tomorrow, and this page will change with them.
816.headline: A new game is here

817.body:
"Hello Money!" has joined the Maryland lineup at $5 with seven top prizes of $50,000. Only on the first day do the printed odds describe the game exactly, because nothing has been won. Starting tomorrow, this page shows how that changes.

Everything above about "Hello Money!" comes from the Maryland Lottery's own published numbers. We only do the counting.
817.headline: New game, all prizes left

818.body:
Of the unclaimed prize money on "10X Cash", most is in wins under $1,000. The game is a game built around small prizes that are won often. That is neither good nor bad, only how it was designed. Choose the kind of game that fits the win you want.

If you play "10X Cash" often, bookmark this page. The write-up is updated with each morning's data.
818.headline: Same price, different prizes

819.body:
"30X Cash" has 319 of 320 top prizes left and is early in its run. Only a small slice of the tickets are already sold. As a game goes on, the same prizes are spread across fewer tickets. Right now, neither the tickets nor the top prizes are running out faster than the other.

Tomorrow's count on "30X Cash" will be a little different. The game sells every day, and this page keeps track.
819.headline: Tickets sold so far
